title: Close cyclic-line span-six dirty-auxiliary cases via the common-J lemma
body:
PR4119 left twelve cyclic off-diagonal lines open for eight rank-one calls at frame span six with three invertible 3×3 data targets and a dirty fourth role. This package reduces all twelve to Ali Romman's existing common-J lemma (PR468 §5.1): a coordinate-only 3+1 triangular split projects the core to J and coordinate calls, while the fourth block receives only its own coordinate calls. The core's relation nullity stays at most two by zero-extension. Total target rank is therefore at most the coordinate-call count, excluding three invertible targets in eight calls without imposing restoration on the arbitrary auxiliary diagonal endpoint.

The result explicitly depends on the retained common-J written lemma. It does not invoke the full three-register computer-assisted theorem or its lower-triangular target restriction. A separate AI-agent mathematical review inspected the exact source lemma and the new proof and found no applicability blocker; this is not human or proof-kernel acceptance. Flagless two-dimensional patterns, span-five families, native legality, physical/compiler/precision costs and supplier admission remain outside scope. No new κ or selected-frontier change.

Validation on CPython3.12.2: registered normal/optimized checks pass; two projector enumerations agree on120 projectors and12 cyclic shapes;300 symbolic pair projections,12 ordered eight-call fixtures, a mixed-relation nullity2→1 calibration, the common-J terminal formula, a nine-call endpoint and five failure controls pass. Final committed-byte/source-history checks and official nine-file export integrity pass; actual Git-free normal/optimized replays pass with all ten exported files (including metadata) unchanged. No Lean, Docker, historical heavy replay or full selected cold replay was run.
